find:
paths = [...await names(["diff-tree", "-r", "--no-renames", "--name-only", "-z", from.commit, target]),
      ...await names(["log", "--no-renames", "--diff-merges=separate", "--name-only", "--format=", "-z", range])];
test: node --test --test-name-pattern='reproducer: a migration in an earlier commit' tests/updater-attended-source.test.mjs
why: the change set is measured from the installed release, not from the target commit's own parent

test: node --test --test-name-pattern='added and reverted inside the update' tests/updater-attended-source.test.mjs
why: every commit in the range counts, so a migration added and reverted inside one update is still a change

test: node --test --test-name-pattern='any file under the updater DDL directory' tests/updater-attended-source.test.mjs
why: the updater's fixed DDL is applied by the release schema phase, which a non-fresh install does not run

test: node --test --test-name-pattern='any file under the updater DDL directory' tests/updater-attended-source.test.mjs
why: the grants, role manifest, ledger and queue data the release schema phase reads live in deploy/postgres
any .sql file is a database change, matching the referee's classes.json database patterns
APFS folds case, so DB/x lands in db/ and must classify like it

test: node --test --test-name-pattern='not an ancestor of the target, or is unknown' tests/updater-attended-source.test.mjs
why: an installed commit that is unknown or not related to the target proves nothing and fails closed

test: node --test --test-name-pattern='not an ancestor of the target, or is unknown' tests/updater-attended-source.test.mjs
why: git's exit 1 means not an ancestor; only exit 0 proves the installed commit is in the target's history

test: node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern='classified from the installed commit' tests/updater-referee.test.ts
why: the referee diffs from the installed release's commit, never from the candidate's own parent
